title: The Centre of Our Galaxy Might Taste Like Raspberries

scenes.text: The centre of our galaxy might taste like raspberries.
Near the heart of the Milky Way sits a giant cloud of gas and dust called Sagittarius B two, where new stars are born.
In two thousand nine, astronomers pointed a radio telescope at it and found a molecule called ethyl formate inside.
Ethyl formate is the chemical that gives raspberries their flavour. It's drifting around in space, about twenty-six thousand light years from the nearest fruit.
It forms because simple molecules stick to tiny icy dust grains and get built up piece by piece into bigger and bigger ones.
The same cloud also holds ethanol, the alcohol in drinks. Raspberries and booze, in the middle of the galaxy. What would space taste like to you?

description:
The centre of our galaxy might taste like raspberries.
In 2009, astronomers using the IRAM radio telescope detected ethyl formate, the molecule that gives raspberries their flavour, in Sagittarius B2, a giant star-forming cloud near the heart of the Milky Way.
Such molecules are built up piece by piece on the surfaces of tiny icy dust grains. The same cloud also contains ethanol, the alcohol found in drinks.
What do you think space would taste like?
